title: A new treatment for preterm pre-eclampsia could benefit mother and child
abstract:
Nature Medicine, Published online: 11 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04400-y

A first-in-human trial involving selective removal of the placental protein sFlt-1 in preterm pre-eclampsia provides critical safety data, and could mark the beginning of a new era of targeted therapy for this potentially lethal pregnancy complication.
headline: Removing a harmful placental protein safely improves outcomes in dangerous pregnancy complications.
why_it_matters: Pre-eclampsia is a life-threatening condition that affects pregnant people and can harm or kill both mother and baby. This is the first human test of a targeted treatment that removes a specific harmful protein, offering hope for safer pregnancies when the condition develops early. If it works, doctors could have a new tool to save lives during high-risk pregnancies.
key_findings: Selective removal of sFlt-1 (a protein made by the placenta that damages blood vessels) was safe in human patients with early-onset pre-eclampsia
The treatment targeted the root cause of the disease rather than just treating symptoms like high blood pressure
This first-in-human trial provided critical safety data needed before larger studies can proceed
The approach could extend pregnancy duration and reduce harm to both mother and developing baby in cases where pre-eclampsia appears early
methods_snapshot: Researchers conducted a first-in-human clinical trial where they selectively removed sFlt-1 protein from the blood of pregnant patients with severe early pre-eclampsia. The team monitored safety and outcomes to see if this targeted approach was tolerable and showed signs of benefit.

glossary.definition: A dangerous pregnancy condition where the mother develops high blood pressure and organ damage, threatening both her life and the baby's
A protein made by the placenta that, in excess, damages blood vessels and causes pre-eclampsia symptoms
Happening before the normal 40-week pregnancy is complete, increasing health risks for the newborn
The organ that connects a developing baby to the mother and supplies oxygen and nutrients
Treatment designed to attack a specific harmful molecule or cause rather than using broad-acting drugs

limitations: This was a small first-in-human safety trial, so results are preliminary and larger studies are needed to confirm effectiveness. The long-term outcomes for babies and mothers and optimal timing of treatment still need investigation.
